key_insight: A steady boundary-driven flux can condense an otherwise stable binary mixture into a stationary inner annulus, with the flux acting as an effective logarithmic field.
engineering_relevance: Boundary permeability and permeate chemical potential offer potential controls for localized phase separation in radial membrane systems.
method: Model B dynamics in a two-dimensional annulus with a semipermeable inner boundary.
Map the driven steady state to an equilibrium profile in an effective logarithmic field.
Derive condensation thresholds, front position, and interfacial-tension effects.
evidence_signal: Numerical solutions confirm the analytical predictions and reveal hysteresis bounded by two saddle-node bifurcations.
watch_item: The results rely on a two-dimensional radial Model B description; applicability with hydrodynamic flow or more complex geometries remains unestablished.
paper_title: Flux-induced condensation in a radial geometry
